## 7. Pattern E — Derive-twice instead of pass-the-value

**Priority 6.** Structurally identical to the incident that triggered this audit: a value is computed correctly in one place and then *re-derived* somewhere else instead of being threaded through.

### Instances

| Site | Re-derived instead of reused |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/tag.rs:51-74` vs `:117-141` | Floating-major tag name: template lookup → version extract → grammar resolve → parse → render → `contains_tag`, written out fully in the dry-run branch and again in the write branch. The module's doc comment says the permit split exists so "the preview branch and the write branch cannot disagree" — the split guarantees only that *a write* doesn't happen, not that the previewed *name* matches. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/status.rs:13-25` | `report.packages.iter().any(|p| !p.pending_changesets.is_empty())` recomputed for the `--check` exit code, while `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/status.rs:105` already computed and stored it as `StatusReport.has_changesets`. JSON output and exit code can disagree. |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/validate.rs:23-66` | `--staged` and `--since` each run their own git diff, error-map, quote-strip, and `ends_with` filter; only the argv differs. |

### Structural fix — plan-then-execute, mechanically

1. `tag.rs`: one pure `fn plan_floating_major(ws, release) -> Result<Option<FloatingMajorPlan>, GraphError>` returning `{ name: TagName, already_existed: bool }`. Preview renders the plan; the write branch consumes the *same* value it was handed. The permit then gates only `git.create_floating_major(plan.name)`.
2. `status.rs`: `check_exit_code_raw` reads `report.has_changesets`. One-line fix; the general rule is *the CLI never recomputes a field the report already carries* — enforceable as a review checklist item and partially by making derived report fields the only public accessor.
3. `validate.rs`: `fn changed_files(runner, root, args: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<String>, GraphError>`; both branches supply argv only.
4. **The general rule worth writing into `AGENTS.md`:** any `if permit.is_some()` / `if dry_run` split must branch on *executing a plan value*, never on *recomputing the plan*. That single sentence describes both this pattern and the original incident.

**Cost:** M (mostly mechanical). **Risk of leaving it:** medium — no live bug found, but this is the incident's exact shape and the release path already has two variants of it (`tag.rs`, and Pattern C's preview command).

**Priority 7.** Security-adjacent, medium cost.

### Instances

- **GitHub owner/repo, three notions, two validators, one crate:**
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release.rs:1009-1014` `is_safe_github_repository` — no character class at all; `"owner name/repo"` passes. Used at `release.rs:923` in `GitHubAttestationPolicyV1::new` — the artifact-attestation provenance boundary.
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/release_pr.rs:394-411` `validate_repository`/`valid_repo_part` — ASCII alnum + `-_.` per part.
  - `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release.rs:1201` — a **third** construction, `format!("{owner}/{repository}")` from a parsed remote URL with no validation, feeding `dispatch_forge_release`.
  - The field is declared as bare `repository: String` in ~6 struct/constructor positions across `release.rs` and `release_pr.rs`.
- **`TagName(pub String)`** (`/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-model/src/tag.rs:163-172`) — unvalidated newtype with a *public* field, so a tag name that looks like a flag is constructible. ### Structural fix — parse, don't validate

```rust
// callisto-model
pub struct GitHubRepository { owner: String, repo: String }   // private fields
impl GitHubRepository {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, InvalidGitHubRepository>; // one charset, one rule
    pub fn as_slug(&self) -> String;   // "owner/repo"
}
```
Replace every `repository: String` in `release.rs`/`release_pr.rs` with `GitHubRepository`; delete both validators; make `release.rs:1201` construct via `parse`. Do the same for `TagName`: private field + `TagName::parse` rejecting leading `-`, control chars, and git's `check-ref-format` illegal sequences. Then the argv `--` becomes defense-in-depth rather than the sole guard.

**Enforcement:** the type system — an unvalidated slug becomes unconstructible.

**Cost:** M (a mechanical type substitution across ~8 fields plus serde round-trip tests). **Risk of leaving it:** medium — the looser validator guards the more security-sensitive boundary, which is the wrong way round.

## 9. Pattern H — Parallel arms over a closed set of kinds

**Priority 8.** Largest code volume, lowest incident probability, highest refactor risk. **Be honest: this one cannot be made structurally impossible — only cheaper.**

### Instances

| Site | Duplicated axis |
|---|---|
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/resolve.rs:350-485` | `[[package]]` vs `[[package-set]]` — same 5 fields, same 5 sub-parsers, same `PackageConfig` literal; differs by pattern parser + error prefix |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs:70-125, 127-222` | fixed vs linked — validation and member resolution, twice |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/locate/membership.rs:34-114` vs `:511-582` | Cargo vs Python membership; comment literally says "Mirrors CargoMembership exactly" |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs:201-243` vs `:612-644`, `:285-377` vs `:646-708` | member manifest vs workspace root — decor-preserving TOML write, twice, incl. the three dependency shapes and the `UnrecognizedDependencyValue` fallback |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-manifests/src/python.rs:220-243, 296-334, 404-455` | PEP 508 decomposition (marker split → first operator → extras split) written from scratch three times — read path can disagree with both write paths |
| `/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-changelog/src/write.rs:60-87` | three header-shape branches with identical 5-statement tails |

### Structural fix — introduce the missing *values*, not a code-sharing scheme

The reason these copies exist is that the thing varying (a group kind, a rule kind, an ecosystem's membership table, a requirement string) has no representation, so the variation is expressed as code structure.

1. **PEP 508 gets a type.** `struct Requirement { name, extras, op_and_spec, marker }` with `parse` / `render` and a round-trip property test. All three sites collapse to `Requirement::parse(s)?` and the read/write disagreement becomes unrepresentable. Natural home: `callisto-format` (Layer 1, permissive) or `callisto-manifests::common`.
2. **TOML decor gets a helper.** `fn set_preserving_decor(item: &mut Item, key: &str, value: Value)` + `fn set_dependency_version(item: &mut Item, v: &str) -> Result<(), ManifestError>` handling the three shapes once. `CargoToml` and `WorkspaceCargoResolver` both call it; the extensive decor test suite in that file then covers one implementation instead of two.
3. **Kind becomes a parameter.** `GroupTable::resolve` takes `GroupKind` and loops `[Fixed, Linked]`; `ResolvedConfig::load` gets `fn resolve_package_config(raw: &RawPackageCommon, kind_label: &str) -> Result<PackageConfig, ConfigError>` called by both loops, so a new `PackageConfig` field is a compile error in exactly one place.
4. **Membership becomes generic.** `struct Membership { members, exclude, hybrid_root }` + `fn read_membership(root, spec: &MembershipSpec)` where `MembershipSpec` names the file and the TOML path. Pairs naturally with Pattern B's `ManifestFormat::CANONICAL`.
5. `write.rs::prepend`: compute `rest` in the if/else, then one shared tail.

**Cost:** L (spread across three crates; `cargo.rs` and `python.rs` have dense test suites that must keep passing byte-for-byte). **Risk of leaving it:** low-medium; no divergence observed today in most of these. **Recommendation: do #1 and #2 (real correctness content), defer #3-#5** unless touched for another reason.

**Confirmed — this is a real bug in my own code from PR #54, verified independently just now.** `document["project"]["version"]` panics (not returns None) when `[project]` doesn't exist — I just reproduced it directly with the exact `toml_edit` version this workspace pins. My `manifest_version_at` in `release_decision.rs` uses this panicking bracket syntax for the Cargo and Pypi branches, and it's called unconditionally for every package in the graph on every `release plan --from-release-commit` run. A Poetry-only `pyproject.toml` (no `[project]` table), a PEP 621 `dynamic = ["version"]` package, or a `Cargo.toml` with no `[package]` table would crash release verification instead of cleanly rejecting it.

This needs fixing now, before PR #54 merges — not deferred to the audit report. Fixing it immediately.

content.text:
Committed and pushed to PR #54.

## Critical finding fixed, now in PR #54

The audit's synthesis surfaced something I verified independently before trusting it: my own `manifest_version_at` (written today, for the persist-and-verify fix) used `toml_edit`'s panicking `Index` operator instead of safe `.get()` chains. I reproduced the panic myself against the exact pinned `toml_edit` version, then fixed it and added two regression tests (one proving no-panic on the previously-crashing shapes, one proving the existing Poetry-fallback and normal-Cargo behavior still works). Clean build, clippy, and tests — now pushed.

## Audit results

12 parallel agents scanned the whole workspace, merged to 32 findings, all 32 survived adversarial verification, then a synthesis pass grouped them into **8 architectural patterns**, ranked by priority:

| # | Pattern | Findings | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| B | No shared manifest *reader* — every crate hand-parses Cargo.toml/package.json/pyproject.toml itself | 6 | **1** (contains the panic just fixed, plus a silent discovery gap for Flit-based Python packages) |
| C | Two generations of the publish/tag pipeline coexist; the live one is *less* capable than the dead one | 3 | **2** (a pnpm/yarn workspace publishes with the wrong tool **today**) |
| D | Fixed/linked group severity math implemented 3x — this is the exact bug class that started this whole session | 2 | **3** (a reachable crash remains for linked groups) |
| G | Credential redaction copy-pasted into 5 crates; a 6th (`callisto-moon`) never got the copy at all | 3 | 4 (security-adjacent, cheap fix) |
| A | 7 traits + 3 config structs are dead abstraction — zero implementations/callers beyond their own definition | 10 | 5 (pure deletion, near-zero risk) |
| E | "Preview vs. write" branches re-derive instead of reusing the same computed value | 4 | 6 |
| F | GitHub repo/tag identity validated inconsistently across call sites (one validator is stricter than the other) | 2 | 7 |
| H | Config/membership parsing duplicated per-kind (package vs package-set, Cargo vs Python) | 6 | 8 |

Full report (structural fixes, workstream sequencing, and a "borderline — needs your call" section for things like whether to delete the dead `PublishOrchestrator` or promote it) is in the workflow transcript. Want it as a proper artifact/document, or should I start opening PRs for the top-priority patterns?
Yes, let's start opening PRs for the high priority issues. Batch whatever makes sense to batch together please
A few of these have real decisions only you can make before I touch them — let me get those first, then start on the unambiguous ones immediately.

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"## Summary
- `derive_release_commit_decision` re-derives the release roster from a merged commit's diff and only recognized a package as authorized when a consumed changeset named it directly. It had no notion that `solve_cascade` sweeps every fixed/linked-group member to one shared converged target the instant any member bumps (Track 1) -- so any real release touching a group failed closed with `E124: release intent no longer matches the current workspace snapshot`, even though the bump was entirely legitimate.
- This repository's own `workspace` fixed group covers 7 of 10 crates with no changeset ever naming them directly, so every release attempt past the first correctly-signed merge hit this. Confirmed by replaying the real failing commit (`7444599d`, [run 34004467492](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/actions/runs/34004467492)) against the fix and getting a correct decision back.
- Also fixes `ReleaseInclusionReason` missing `rename_all_fields = "camelCase"` (the same `rename_all`-does-not-rename-variant-fields gap already fixed for `ReleasePrActionV1`) -- it was serializing `group_id`/`edge_kind`/`policy_id` as snake_case. Caught by writing this fix's own test, which asserted `groupId` and failed against the unfixed serialization.

## Why / design
The fix expands `selected` (changeset-named packages) into `authorized` via the workspace's `GroupTable.fixed_of`/`linked_of` reverse lookups -- a package triggers its group's inclusion, and every sibling in that group becomes authorized too -- **without re-running the full dependency cascade solver**. This is sufficient and no more permissive than needed: every fixed/linked group member is guaranteed by `solve_cascade` to converge on one identical target version, an invariant checkable directly from the diff alone. A new `E155` (`ReleaseCommitCascadeDivergent`) still fails closed if a triggered group's members disagree on target version, catching a tampered or malformed commit that a real release could never produce.

Dependency-driven `Cascade` and `PreReleasePolicy` bumps remain unsupported and still fail closed, unchanged from before -- this function only re-derives the two cascade shapes that are independently verifiable from the diff.

No test in the repository exercised a fixed/linked group at all before this change (`release_commit_fixture` uses a deliberately single-package workspace). Added `fixed_group_release_commit_fixture` plus two e2e tests (authorized-cascade happy path, divergence rejection) and a unit test for the camelCase fix.

content.text:
Found something real. My `derive_release_commit_decision` in #54 has zero access to `GroupTable`/group membership at all — confirmed via grep, the only hits are in a different, unrelated function. That means PR #53's `E155` check (reject a commit whose claimed fixed-group siblings disagree on target version) has **no equivalent in #54**.

Here's the honest breakdown:

- **Core bug fix, camelCase fix, happy-path test** — fully superseded, verified equivalent or better (my own new e2e test proves the exact original bug scenario now works).
- **`E155` divergence check** — not carried forward, and it's not an accident of oversight in the sense of "I forgot a line of code." It's a real consequence of the architecture change: PR #53 re-derived group membership from the diff itself, so it *had* to independently verify internal consistency (two fixed-group siblings claiming different versions). #54 never re-derives group membership — it trusts the persisted decision's digest as sole authority, the same way it already trusts changeset selection and cascade computation without re-validating *those* either. So by design, #54 would silently accept a self-consistent (valid-digest) decision that internally claims two same-fixed-group packages target different versions, each matching its own manifest diff.

Is that a real problem? To reach it, an attacker would need to forge a decision file with a matching SHA-256 digest — which means either running the real `plan_version` (which can never produce divergent group targets, so this path is closed) or hand-computing the digest against arbitrary entries (requires understanding/reproducing the exact canonical-transcript hash, a nontrivial forgery, and they'd already need commit access to a branch that passes GitHub's signed-merge trust check to matter at all). So it's a narrow, defense-in-depth gap, not an open door — but I have zero test coverage proving that's actually true rather than assumed. Want me to add a test that pins this down explicitly, so the trust boundary is verified rather than implicit?

## Summary
- `ReleaseDecisionV1::new` now rejects a decision claiming divergent target versions for two entries tagged with the same `FixedGroup`/`LinkedGroup` `group_id`.
- The check reads only the decision's own entries and their self-declared group reasons -- no `GroupTable`/workspace access needed.
- Since the digest-validating `Deserialize` impl calls `new()` internally, this also closes the same gap at merge-commit-verification time (a decision read back from a committed release-decision file), not just for a decision freshly derived from a version plan.

## Why
A fixed or linked group always converges every member to one shared target version -- `solve_cascade` guarantees this whenever a decision is legitimately derived. This PR was originally a different, larger fix for the same underlying concern (re-deriving group membership from a merged commit's raw diff and checking divergence there); that approach was superseded by #54's persist-and-verify redesign, which made the re-derivation itself unnecessary.

What #54 didn't cover: its merge-commit verifier trusts a persisted, digest-verified decision as sole authority and never consults live group config, so nothing previously checked that a decision's own claims about a fixed/linked group's members were internally consistent. A hand-forged (but digest-self-consistent) decision claiming two same-group packages target different versions would have been silently accepted. This closes that gap, entirely within `ReleaseDecisionV1`'s own invariants rather than needing graph-layer group lookups.

## Test Plan
- [x] `cargo test -p callisto-model --lib release::tests` -- 20/20 pass, including 4 new tests (fixed-group divergence rejected, linked-group divergence rejected, agreeing versions accepted, divergence rejected on deserialize with a self-consistent digest)
- [x] `cargo clippy -p callisto-model --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
- [x] `cargo build --workspace` clean
EOF
)"

input.title: Forked subagent mimics parent's own status narration instead of executing its task
input.details:
**What happened:** Launched `subagent_type: "fork"` twice (isolation: worktree) with a large, fully self-contained implementation task (refactor + build + test + git commit + PR). No worktree/branch was ever created either time.
**What the user said:** User didn't comment on this specific failure; observed by the model mid-session.
**Repro:** Long conversation with many recent turns consisting mostly of "waiting on background task X" status updates (repeated cargo build/test polling). Then call Agent with subagent_type "fork" for a substantial, unrelated implementation task. The fork's first (and often only) action appears to be reproducing the parent's narration style rather than engaging with the actual prompt.
**Evidence:** Two agent runs in the same session, ids ending `...4f827` and `...4b469`; both `tool_uses: 1`, durations 20863ms and 11405ms.
**Cause:** Suspected: fork inherits full conversation context, and a context dominated by repeated short "waiting on X" status turns may bias the model toward continuing that pattern rather than treating the new prompt as a distinct task, even when the prompt explicitly says to ignore that narration.
